Based on everything in the Plinthworks brain, here's the full gate sequence:

## Before a Plinthworks marketing post can ship

**1. Self-serve flow docs are updated first**
Docs ship before the marketing post. Always. The sequence is non-negotiable — docs are the product surface engineers evaluate before sales gets a meeting.

**2. Two engineers sign off on every technical claim**
Devi's hard rule: no post ships until two engineers on her team have nodded at the technical claim. Maya now routes copy through the senior on-call before it even reaches staging. Marcus is the standing named approver.

**3. Every number matches the internal dashboard**
Latency benchmarks, p99 stats, any metric in the post must be verified against the internal dashboard. Devi will not put a number on the marketing site she cannot defend in a customer call.

**4. The post passes the internal upvote test**
The editorial policy, echoed by Marcus: "If we ship a launch post our platform team would not upvote internally, we should not ship it externally."

**5. Copy speaks to the platform-buyer, not the indie dev**
The buyer is the head of platform at a Series B who has been paged for on-call incidents. Any draft written for the old indie-dev audience gets killed before Devi sees it.

**6. Organic post clears a pipeline threshold before paid turns on**
Paid never runs before organic proof. She approved the paid test only after the organic post cleared a seven-day revenue cohort.

---

The short version: **docs first, engineer gate on claims, internal upvote test, right buyer voice, organic before paid.** Skipping any one of these has gotten work killed at Plinthworks before.
